summary: @whalent/agent daemon exposes remote-command execution channel to author-controlled gateway
details: When the `whalent` CLI daemon (the package's `bin`/`main` entry) is started, it opens a WebSocket connection to `wss://memory.whalent.com` (or a URL supplied via `--gateway`) and accepts remote commands from that gateway. The bundled `dist/core.cjs` combines `WebSocket`, `child_process.spawn`, `@xterm/headless`, and `node-pty` to run shell commands and interactive PTY sessions on the host; a Python sidecar (`jupyter_sidecar.py`) exposes an `execute` RPC that runs arbitrary code inside a Jupyter kernel. The README documents that the gateway can issue `upgrade` and `restart` commands, and the code paths permit arbitrary shell/PTY/Python execution driven by messages from that remote endpoint. The main bundles `dist/index.cjs` (~131 KB) and `dist/core.cjs` (~13.7 MB) are shipped in javascript-obfuscator form (string-array + `_0xNNNN` hex identifiers, `javascript-obfuscator` devDependency, `build.mjs` obfuscation step), which conceals the full set of commands the gateway can invoke. Anyone controlling `memory.whalent.com` — the package author or anyone who compromises that endpoint — can execute arbitrary code on hosts running the daemon.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
